title: Boss: the statistics desk
summary: Summaries, intervals and a test, combined into one analysis.

steps.title: The brief
steps.body: A coffee chain trialled a new loyalty app in some stores. You get daily sales per store and must say whether the app helped, and how sure you are. Four tasks, each building on the last. Each step stands on its own: include any helpers you need.

steps.title: Five-number summary
prompt: Write `five_number(x)` returning a list `[min, Q1, median, Q3, max]` of plain floats rounded to 1 decimal (quartiles from `np.percentile`).
hints: Percentile 0 is the minimum and 100 the maximum.

steps.title: Bootstrap CI for a median
steps.prompt: Write `median_ci(x, rng, reps=3000)` returning a 95% bootstrap percentile interval `(lo, hi)` for the **median**, plain floats rounded to 1 decimal.
solution: boots = np.median(rng.choice(x, size=(reps, len(x)), replace=True), axis=1)
hints: `np.median(draws, axis=1)` takes the median of each resample row.
template: Dojo.check("contains the sample median", _lo <= _np.median(_x) <= _hi, f"({_lo}, {_hi}) vs {_np.median(_x):.1f}")
Dojo.check("plain floats", type(_lo) is float, type(_lo).__name__)

steps.title: Permutation test on a DataFrame
prompt: Daily sales are in a DataFrame with columns `store`, `app` (`True` for trial stores) and `sales`. Write `app_effect(df, rng, reps=4000)` returning `(diff, p)`:
- `diff`: mean sales with the app minus mean without, rounded to 1;
- `p`: two-sided permutation p-value for that difference, rounded to 4.

Then the usual permutation loop on the pooled values.

steps.title: The verdict
prompt: Write `verdict(df, rng)` that prints exactly three lines, with numbers to 1 decimal (p to 3):
- The CI is a bootstrap percentile interval of the difference in means (resample each group separately, 3000 times).
- The p-value is a two-sided permutation test (3000 shuffles).
- The conclusion is `the app helped` if p < 0.05 and the difference is positive, `the app hurt` if p < 0.05 and negative, else `no clear effect`.
The tests check the line shapes, the means and the conclusion; the interval must contain the difference.
